## What worked
- Test-only delta made security triage and scoping quick. Neutral brief with repeated first-call rules; both reviewers finished (Sol 5 min, Opus about 12 min) and agreed by different methods (source-only vs sealed mutant runs).

## Process deviations (candid)
- Coordinator: one policy read used `cut -c1-2000` (a width projection). Measured max line length in that range was 1009, so no content was truncated, but the form violated the no-projection rule.
- Coordinator: a python one-liner printed a large team-registry dict (history with local paths); output exceeded the tool limit and was persisted by the CLI as native tool-result storage outside the assignment (content: team-2.json registry history). Preserved, not deleted. Fix: extract only named fields.
- Opus reviewer: several parallel read batches exceeded the 60-line aggregate per response (no single read over 50 lines, nothing truncated). Brief stated the aggregate rule; consider phrasing it as "one read per tool response" to prevent parallel batching.
- Opus reviewer generated mutant files on the host with a Python substitution script (no PR code executed); all syntax checks and runs were inside review.py.
- Sol's suggested public text included thanking the author; not used (pleasantries are excluded).

## Improvements
- Coordinator STATUS helper for field-only registry reads.
- Brief template: forbid parallel read batches explicitly.
